## Stability\
Updates are never installed without your say-so unless you turn on automatic upgrades. After an upgrade, gbrain shows a one-time notice listing what changed in behaviour. Stable also comes with a written promise about which commands, flags, tools, config keys and output fields stay the same, and how much warning you get before one changes. [docs/STABILITY.md](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/STABILITY.md) explains that promise, how often stable moves, how to pin a version or go back, and what the faster alpha channel is for.

Tip

One command launches a GBrain hosted on gbrain.io; Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor and every other AI you use connect to it, with nothing to keep online.

```
curl -sSL https://gbrainio.terminalwire.sh | bash
gbrainio terminal connect      # in a new terminal
gbrainio workspace new         # pick a plan in the browser
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash   # skip if Bun 1.4.4+ is installed
export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable   # the gbrain CLI only; no local brain
# Claude Code (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
(claude mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || claude mcp add --transport http --scope user gbrain https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup claude-code --instructions-only
# Codex (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
(codex mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || codex mcp add gbrain --url https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup codex --instructions-only
```

## Here's how to self-host it
GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host.

## 1. Run with an agent platform
Already running [OpenClaw](https://github.com/garrytan/openclaw) or [Hermes](https://github.com/garrytan/hermes)?

```
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding   # keyless; no server
gbrain skillpack scaffold --harness openclaw --workspace <ws>   # OpenClaw: the five-skill brain-first core
gbrain skillpack scaffold --all       # Hermes or any other workspace: every bundled skill (skills/manifest.json)
gbrain doctor                         # inspect diagnostics and expected empty-brain warnings
```

## Memory-only upgrades
```
GBRAIN_NO_AUTOPILOT_INSTALL=1 GBRAIN_NO_REEMBED=1 gbrain upgrade --no-autopilot-install
```

## 2. CLI standalone
```
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding
```

**Reinstalled over an existing brain?** The first gbrain command applies schema migrations, and when upgrade migrations are still pending it says so with the command that runs them ( [#218](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/218)): `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --no-autopilot-install`. Run `gbrain doctor` if that exits 1. The deterministic fallback is `git clone https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain.git ~/gbrain && cd ~/gbrain && GBRAIN_NO_AUTOPILOT_INSTALL=1 bun install && bun link`.",

## Step 1: Install GBrain
Install only `github:garrytan/gbrain#stable` `github:garrytan/gbrain` installs master) or a git clone, as below.

```
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable
```

```
arch=$(uname -m); [ "$arch" = x86_64 ] && arch=x64; [ "$arch" = arm64 ] && arch=aarch64
mkdir -p ~/.bun/bin
curl -fsSL "https://registry.npmjs.org/@oven/bun-linux-$arch/-/bun-linux-$arch-1.4.4.tgz" | tar -xzO package/bin/bun > ~/.bun/bin/bun.new && chmod +x ~/.bun/bin/bun.new && ~/.bun/bin/bun.new --version && mv ~/.bun/bin/bun.new ~/.bun/bin/bun
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile
export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable
bash -lc 'gbrain --version'
```

Don't install Bun with `npm install -g bun` or run gbrain from a git clone instead: gbrain starts with `#!/usr/bin/env bun`, so it fails in any new shell that can't find `bun` on its PATH.

```
git clone --branch stable https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain.git ~/gbrain && cd ~/gbrain
bun install && bun link
```

        "description": "# Stability: which gbrain you get and how it changes
## What the default install gives you
The install command in the README, `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable`, installs the current stable release. `git clone --branch stable` does the same. A new brain created by `gbrain init` (no earlier config file) is set to the stable channel, and an install with no channel set follows stable too. Every update path follows the channel in effect: the update notice, `gbrain check-update`, `gbrain upgrade`, `gbrain self-upgrade` and the opt-in automatic upgrades.

Check which channel you are on with `gbrain doctor`, which prints `channel=<channel>` when one is set.

## How often stable moves
```
git ls-remote --tags --refs https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain 'refs/tags/stable-v*'
```

## Staying on stable
```
gbrain config set self_upgrade.channel stable
gbrain upgrade --dry-run --json   # what an upgrade would install, installing nothing
```

## Going back to an earlier release
```
git ls-remote --exit-code --tags https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain refs/tags/v<previous> >/dev/null && \
  { ! bun pm ls -g 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'gbrain@' || bun remove -g gbrain; } && \
  bun add -g --backend=copyfile github:garrytan/gbrain#v<previous>
```
